reference_sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.store_id, s.store_code
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-05 00:00:00'
alternatives: SELECT o.order_id, s.store_id, s.store_code FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-04'
SELECT order_id, store_id, store_code FROM orders JOIN stores USING (store_id) WHERE CAST(order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-04'

other_way.sql: SELECT order_id, store_id, store_code FROM orders JOIN stores USING (store_id) WHERE CAST(order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-04'
other_way.tradeoff: USING merges the shared column into one, so no alias is needed, but both tables must give it the same name.
